loci.name: caged-judge-protocol-for-grounded-replies
loci.one_line: Which rubric + mitigation + human-anchor bundle makes an LLM judge trustworthy for groundedness, resolution-usefulness, and escalation-appropriateness?
loci.rationale: The assignment demands judge-human agreement evidence; the corpus's tightest fight is judge usability. Resolving the exact cage (dimensions, swap/length controls, separate-model judge, correlation + kappa targets, disagreement analysis) fixes the evaluation chapter's core design.

loci.name: setfit-vs-llm-intent-with-uncertainty-routing
loci.one_line: Can SetFit-first with MC-dropout uncertainty routing to an LLM match native-LLM few-shot intent accuracy on noisy Twitter text at a fraction of cost and latency?
loci.rationale: Determines the classifier architecture and the cost/latency story of the whole submission; both sides have controlled numbers (56x speed, within-2% hybrid, Banking77 LLM wins). Needs OOS-behavior and label-scope reading to set taxonomy guidance.

loci.name: leakage-safe-temporal-split-vs-random-stratified-split
loci.one_line: Does the golden set and eval need conversation-disjoint temporal splits, or does random stratified sampling suffice?
loci.rationale: Leakage audit is the assignment's top trust killer (same-thread overlap, retrieval of the target response, future-data answering past messages). The split design decides whether headline numbers mean anything.

loci.name: escalation-calibration-under-shift
loci.one_line: What confidence signal, held-out threshold procedure, and risk-coverage reporting justify auto-handle vs escalate given MaxProb robustness and over-abstention costs?
loci.rationale: Escalation is a graded deliverable (decision + reason); the corpus disagrees on whether anything beats MaxProb. Resolving the floor (MaxProb + temperature scaling + calibration split + AURC) vs learned calibrator sets the policy chapter.

loci.name: hybrid-retrieval-payoff-on-identifier-heavy-tweets
loci.one_line: How much does BM25+dense fusion with cross-encoder rerank beat pure dense on identifier/handle/noise-heavy support tweets, and at what latency and complexity cost?
loci.rationale: Retrieval grounds every reply; Twitter support text is the worst case for pure dense (short, noisy, identifier-heavy). The margin decides whether hybrid complexity is justified or over-engineering.

loci.name: golden-set-adjudication-and-agreement-gate
loci.one_line: What agreement metric thresholds and adjudication rules certify the 150-250 golden set before any headline metric is quoted?
loci.rationale: Golden-set validity gates every number in the report; the corpus agrees on the machinery (guidelines, kappa/alpha, adjudication) but not the gates. Sets sampling strata + agreement bar + disagreement-handling procedure.
